Sell the copyist what he came for.
Decide where the map ends up.

quests.name: What Came Ashore
quests.description: The Portion of Grace went onto the bar in the Lastmonth blow. Most of her is on the Bone Beach and some of what came off her has not settled.

stages.name: Walk the Bone Beach
stages.description: Four hundred years of ribs and stem-posts at every angle, and a new one among them still wet.

objectives.description: Walk out to the Bone Beach.

stages.name: What is still coming up the shingle
stages.description: They came off the reef with the cargo and did not stop at the tide line.

objectives.description: Put down what came ashore with her.

stages.name: Tell the Wreckmaster
stages.description: He sent you out. He will want it said to his face.

objectives.description: Report to Orl.

quests.name: The Lime Kiln
quests.description: Cass keeps the burner's hut and the kiln has been cold for sixty years, and on the night of the blow it was not.

objectives.description: Get up to the lime kiln.
See what the draw-hole was used for.
Ask Cass who lit her kiln.

quests.name: The Run Under the Strand
quests.description: A fire on the kiln at four miles reads as a harbour light, and whatever came off the Grace before she broke did not go up the beach. It went under it.

stages.name: Find the run
stages.description: It goes in at the back of the beach and comes out somewhere up on the downs, which is the whole point of it.

objectives.description: Get into the Smugglers' Cave.

stages.name: Who is holding it
stages.description: Two men who did not expect the far end to be walked from this direction, and one thing that was already down here.

objectives.description: Clear the far end of the run.

quests.name: A Share or a Name
quests.description: The cargo is under the downs, the kiln was lit on purpose, and two people would like to hear about it in two very different rooms.

objectives.description: Take the Strand's share and say nothing.
Give the Insurers' Hall a name.
Settle what happens to the cargo.

quests.name: The Wrong Light
quests.description: Four hulls in nine years, all of them insured at the Hall, all of them certain they had the Saltcliff Light fine on the bow when they struck. Maun would like somebody to go and ask the keeper.

objectives.description: Climb to the Saltcliff Light.
Ask Bry what his logbook says.
Hear what he has stopped reporting.

quests.name: The Ledger
quests.description: Bry's logbook says the light was out on two of the four nights, which is worse than saying it was lit. The findings of the Harbour Court will say what the Hall paid and to whom.

objectives.description: Get into the Harbour Court.
Find what the four findings have in common.
Take the pattern back to Maun.

quests.name: Under the Light
quests.description: All four struck within an hour of the low, and the low is when the chalk workings under the Rise are dry to the back. Something is getting up to the head from underneath.

stages.name: Into the workings
stages.description: Pillar and stall, quarried out to build the town, and the town is now standing on the hole.

objectives.description: Get into the Chalk Workings.

stages.name: What has been showing
stages.description: Ninety years off one headland, and the lighthouse is not it.

objectives.description: Put out the light on the point.

quests.name: The Finding
quests.description: There is a finding to be written, and what it says decides whether the Strand has been paying for ninety years of something it did not do.

objectives.description: File the finding as it stands.
Let the old findings stand.
See the finding written.

quests.name: What Wend Has Been Saying
quests.description: Two years of messages to Elderhollow about the beeches moving, and two years of the moot having something more pressing on.

objectives.description: Find the hermit in the Hollow Beeches.
Hear what he has been trying to tell the moot.
Count the ring with him.

quests.name: The Root Cellar
quests.description: There is a cellar under the King, which is the largest of the beeches, and Wend says it is not a cellar and never was.

objectives.description: Get into the root cellar.
See what the tree grew around.
Take it back to Wend.

quests.name: The Deadfall
quests.description: Whatever was put in that hole was put in it by people who then planted a wood on top, and the wood has been doing the job since. One of them has stopped.

stages.name: Out along the Thornback Ride
stages.description: The narrows, and then the deadfall, which is where the foresters stopped working and did not write down why.

objectives.description: Reach the Deadfall Cave.

stages.name: What the beech grew around
stages.description: Four hundred years growing round a hole somebody dug, and it has taken the shape of what it grew around.

objectives.description: Put down the Hollow Beech.

quests.name: Fire or Graft
quests.description: It can be burnt out in an afternoon, and the Greenway is four hundred years old and joined at the root.

objectives.description: Graft the ring back and let it close slowly.
Burn the deadfall out.
Settle what happens to the ring.

quests.name: The West End
quests.description: Pell has eleven diggers, a fellow's warrant, and a west end that has started giving things back that were not put in it.

stages.name: The camp on the ridge
stages.description: Eleven on day rates and four of them not turning up.

objectives.description: Reach the diggers' camp.

stages.name: What is coming up the cutting
stages.description: The spoil heap is on the wrong side of the trench and something has been walking it at night.

objectives.description: Clear the west cutting.

stages.name: Tell Pell
stages.description: She will want it described rather than summarised.

objectives.description: Report to Pell.

quests.name: The Ridge
quests.description: Four hundred feet of barrow with two ends, and everything anybody has ever dug has been at the western one. Pell wants the reason walked rather than read.

objectives.description: Walk the length of the ridge.
See what the barrow is pointed at.
Ask Pell what lines up with the east end.

quests.name: The East End
quests.description: The east end was never dug, and it was never dug on purpose, and the moot has written twice to say which of those two facts is load-bearing.

stages.name: Open the east end
stages.description: Two days with eleven men and it is open in an afternoon once they find the kerb.

objectives.description: Get into the east end.

stages.name: Whoever is in it
stages.description: Buried facing the other way from everybody else, and crowned, which nobody in this parish has ever been.

objectives.description: Put down what is in the east end.

quests.name: Record or Rebury
quests.description: It is open, and it can be written down or it can be closed, and there is not time before the weather to do both properly.

objectives.description: Let the Library have its record.
Close the east end the way the moot asked.
Decide what the east end becomes.

quests.name: The Third Well
quests.description: Three Wells has two. The third went in a season nine years ago and Saray has swept it every month since on the grounds that it might come back.

objectives.description: Reach the wells at Three Wells.
Hear what Saray thinks happened to the third.
Look down the dry one.

quests.name: The Lost Wagons
quests.description: Water does not stop. It goes somewhere else. Saray says find where, and says it in the tone of somebody who already knows and would rather be told by a stranger.

objectives.description: Get out into the Long Grass.
See what line the wagons are in.
Take the line back to Saray.

quests.name: Down the Dry Well
quests.description: Eleven wagons in a line, pointed at a well that stopped in the same season, and nothing between the two but grass that grows a different colour.

stages.name: Down the third well
stages.description: Ninety feet of dressed stone, dry to the bottom and dry a good way past it.

objectives.description: Get down the dry well.

stages.name: What is in the bed
stages.description: The river went somewhere else in somebody's great-grandfather's time and something stayed in the bed waiting for it.

objectives.description: Put down what is holding the water.

quests.name: A Road or a Right
quests.description: The well is coming back, and there is a surveyed route to it in your hand that the Crown has wanted for four hundred years.

objectives.description: Give the route to the lines.
Sell the survey to the Crown.
Settle who has the road.

quests.name: The Red Water
quests.description: Nine days red, then two days of nothing at all, and eleven miles down the Kingsvale drinks whatever this mountain decides to send it.

objectives.description: Climb to the corrie lake.
See how far down the colour goes.
Take it back to Hulf at the ward.

quests.name: The Quarry Galleries
quests.description: The Cut was quarried for the Hold road and the galleries run back into the mountain further than the road ever needed. Something has come down them as far as the toll ruin.

stages.name: Into the galleries
stages.description: Driven for stone, and driven a great deal further than stone accounts for.

objectives.description: Get into the quarry galleries.

stages.name: What has come down them
stages.description: Grey, slow, and walking a circuit it did not choose.

objectives.description: Clear the galleries.

quests.name: The Sink
quests.description: The galleries and the swallet are the same hole approached from two sides, and the Hold's ledgers have said so since the year eleven without anybody putting the two pages together.

stages.name: Down the sink
stages.description: Where the Weirwater goes in, and where for two days this spring it did not.

objectives.description: Get down into the Sink.

stages.name: What has never needed to leave
stages.description: In goes at the swallet, out eleven miles down. Something in between has never had a reason to do either.

objectives.description: Put down what is in the Sink.

quests.name: Seal It or Open It
quests.description: The galleries come out on the far side of the pass, which the muleteers have wanted for two hundred years and the Hold has refused for the same two hundred.

objectives.description: Seal the galleries behind you.
Leave the under-road open.
Settle what happens to the Cut.

quests.name: Gone Quiet
quests.description: The chain over the Great Vent has hung still for eleven days. It has never hung still for more than two.

objectives.description: Get out to the chain over the Great Vent.
Hear what the eleven make of it.
See the chain for yourself.

quests.name: The Signal Deep
quests.description: The readers have kept every reading since the hold was cut, and they kept them in the one place nobody would think to burn: a gallery under the firewatch towers, with the numbers on the wall.

objectives.description: Find the Signal Deep under Firewatch Ridge.
Read what the wall has been saying.
Take the two matching years back to Ilka.

quests.name: Down the Throat
quests.description: Twice in nine hundred years the chain has hung still, and both times the wall says the same thing was in the throat, and both times somebody went down and stopped it.

stages.name: Into the Throat
stages.description: Nobody has been down the Throat in four hundred years and the last one who did left the rope.

objectives.description: Get down into the Throat.

stages.name: What has been keeping it quiet
stages.description: Nine hundred years of the vent going gently, and the reason it went gently.

objectives.description: Put down what is in the Throat.

quests.name: Heed It or Haul It
quests.description: The chain is moving again and the reading is worse than it was. There are forty tons of ore in the foundry shed and a contract with Karn Dolur under them.

objectives.description: Sound the reading and stop the works.
Let the foundry finish the contract.
Make the call.

quests.name: The New Tower
quests.description: Gost has lost two poles and a cousin since Harvest, all three in the same reach, and all three on nights the ringers say nothing at all was rung.

objectives.description: Get up to the new tower at Drowned Bell.
Ask Gost what the ringers will not discuss.
Hear what the ringers deny.

quests.name: The Black Water
quests.description: Everything Gost has lost went in the same reach, and the reach has a hall in it with its roof out of the water, which nobody built there.

objectives.description: Get out into the Black Water.
See what is standing in the reach.
Take it back to Gost.

quests.name: The Old Church
quests.description: The hall in the black water is four hundred yards from where the old church went down, and the marsh has been quietly moving one of them towards the other.

stages.name: Out to the old church
stages.description: Roof above, floor a long way under, and the tower still standing because it was built to.

objectives.description: Reach the old church.

stages.name: What has been ringing it
stages.description: One note, under the water, and it is in your chest before it is in your ears.

objectives.description: Silence what rings the bell.

quests.name: Raise It or Sink It
quests.description: The bell is still down there and it is still bell-bronze, and there are two entirely reasonable things to do about that.

objectives.description: Sink it properly and mark the reach.
Raise it for the new tower.
Settle what happens to the bell.

quests.name: The Missing Year
quests.description: The Hold writes down the weather. It has not written down which year it stopped working the old seams, and Vare has spent eleven years being professionally troubled by that.

objectives.description: Reach the Hall of Measures.
Hear what Vare cannot find.
Understand what an omission means here.

quests.name: The Ledger Stone
quests.description: Every fee the Hold has ever charged is cut into the stone at the gatehall, in order, and a fee is charged every year without exception, and Vare would like somebody who is not of the Hold to go and read it.

objectives.description: Get to the ledger stone at the gatehall.
Find the gap in the fees.
Take the years back to Vare.

quests.name: Into the Old Workings
quests.description: Four years with no fee cut, four hundred years ago, in the middle of an unbroken run of nine hundred. The Hold did not charge because the Hold did not open the gate, and it did not open the gate because of what was in the seams behind it.

stages.name: Into the old seams
stages.description: Sealed at the ninth level and not sealed well, which for Karn Dolur is the loudest thing in the chain.

objectives.description: Get into the Old Seams.

stages.name: What stopped the working
stages.description: Karn Dolur stopped working these in the year four hundred and has never written down which year it stopped for.

objectives.description: Put down what is in the old seams.

quests.name: Cut It or Close It
quests.description: Four years are missing from the stone and there is room to cut them in, and a hold that has been right for nine hundred years has an opinion about being publicly wrong for four of them.

objectives.description: Cut the four missing years into the stone.
Seal the seams and leave the stone as it is.
Settle what the Hold admits to.

quests.name: The Second Gallery
quests.description: Two hundred years of holding the line at the fifth. Kesk has been driven back to the second in a season and the beds she has left will not feed Lantern Deep past Highsun.

stages.name: Down to Mycelt
stages.description: Four hundred people, and every one of them growing what nine hundred more eat.

objectives.description: Reach the beds at Mycelt.

stages.name: Cut it back
stages.description: The Rot walks when it is thick enough, which the pickers have known for two hundred years and never had to say to an outsider before.

objectives.description: Cut the gallery back.

stages.name: Tell Kesk
stages.description: She will want the count, and she will do the arithmetic in front of you.

objectives.description: Report to Kesk.

quests.name: The Listening Room
quests.description: The Rot is coming from somewhere and it is coming faster than it grows. The Echo Halls have a room cut to hear the whole length of the Long Hall, and nobody has sat in it in living memory.

objectives.description: Get into the listening room.
Hear what the room is for.
Take what you heard back to Kesk.

quests.name: What Grows Mycelt
quests.description: Not spreading. Being fed. Something up the fungus gallery has been growing the beds for two hundred years and has stopped being careful about the distinction.

stages.name: Up the fungus gallery
stages.description: Past the pickers' camp, past the canopy, and past the point where anybody has cut in two hundred years.

objectives.description: Reach the Rot.

stages.name: What has been growing it
stages.description: Mycelt grows what the Deeproads eat. This grows Mycelt.

objectives.description: Put down the Rot.

quests.name: Burn It or Farm It
quests.description: What is left of it will regrow, and the pickers have spent two hundred years learning exactly how to make that happen on purpose.

objectives.description: Burn the gallery out for good.
Keep a cutting and grow the beds from it.
Settle what happens to the beds.

quests.name: Eight and One
quests.description: Nine shafts at Bone Wells. Eight are on the roster and drawn from daily. The ninth is on the survey, has never been on the roster, and the camp is laid out so that nobody faces it.

objectives.description: Reach the diggers' camp at Bone Wells.
Hear why Sefa was posted out here.
See the roster and the survey side by side.

quests.name: The Milepost Vault
quests.description: The crew that sank the nine came up the Sunken Road, and the Sunken Road has vaults under its mileposts that the caravanserai has been storing barley in for two hundred years.

objectives.description: Find the vault under the milepost.
Read what the original survey counts.
Take the survey back to Sefa.

quests.name: Down the Ninth
quests.description: The survey does not say the ninth failed to find water. It says the ninth was sunk to a depth, which is a different kind of sentence, and it gives the depth.

stages.name: Down the ninth shaft
stages.description: Four hundred feet of dressed stone in a desert, sunk by people who knew exactly how far down they were going.

objectives.description: Get down the ninth well.

stages.name: What is at the depth
stages.description: Eight wells were sunk for water. This one was sunk for something else.

objectives.description: Put down what is at the bottom.

quests.name: Cap It or Open It
quests.description: There is water at the bottom of the ninth after all — a great deal of it, under everything, and Vashta Qal has been rationing one spring for four hundred years.

objectives.description: Put the ninth on the roster.
Cap the ninth and say nothing.
Settle what happens to the water.

quests.name: What the Ice Gave Back
quests.description: The glacier gave back a body this spring with a moot-mark cut into the shoulder, forty miles from anywhere a moot-marked body has any business being.

objectives.description: Reach the cairns at Cairnhold.
Hear what the ice gave back.
See the mark on the shoulder.

quests.name: The Frozen Ship
quests.description: A body in a glacier came off the top of it, and the top of the White Reach has one thing on it that anybody has ever found: a ship, in the middle of the ice, forty miles from water.

objectives.description: Find the frozen ship on the White Reach.
See which way she is pointed.
Take the bearing back to Ottir.

quests.name: Under the Last Cairn
quests.description: Eleven hundred cairns, counted from one, and the ship is pointed straight at it. The Ice Moot has been measuring nine hundred years of work against a thing it has never once opened.

stages.name: Out past the flats
stages.description: Four days from the last roof, and the last day of it into the wind.

objectives.description: Reach the Last Cairn.

stages.name: What it has been holding
stages.description: Nine hundred years of counting from a thing nobody has opened, and one very good reason for that.

objectives.description: Put down what the Last Cairn held.

quests.name: Set It or Move It
quests.description: The cairn can be set back exactly as it was, which is nine hundred years of practice. It can also be moved, which the moot has never done and has a word for.

objectives.description: Set the Last Cairn back as it was.
Move the count to a new first cairn.
Settle what the moot counts from.

quests.name: Four Crews
quests.description: Guns run out and a dry magazine, in one night, and four crews since who went to find out which of those two things happened first.

objectives.description: Reach the hulks at Blackrigging.
Hear Runa's list.
Hear what the one who came out said.

quests.name: The Chimney
quests.description: He came out at Gullstone, which is a mile and a half from the fort and eighty feet above it, and no salvor in four generations has been able to say how.

objectives.description: Get to the bottom of the Gullstone chimney.
See what the chimney is connected to.
Take it back to Runa.

quests.name: The Battery
quests.description: The chimney is a chimney because something under the Narrows needed a draught, and the fort was built on top of it by people who did not know that and worked it out on the last night.

stages.name: In at the hatch
stages.description: Dry inside, which after four hundred years under the passage is the part nobody has ever been able to explain.

objectives.description: Get into the Drowned Fort.

stages.name: The battery floor
stages.description: The guns are still run out and still pointed at the passage, and something down there is still minding them.

objectives.description: Clear the battery floor.

quests.name: Salvage It or Seal It
quests.description: Four hundred years of a fort nobody has been into, dry, with its armoury intact — and a chimney at the far end of it that goes somewhere the Isles would rather not have a road to.

objectives.description: Open the fort to the salvors.
Seal the chimney and leave the fort.
Settle what happens to the fort.

quests.name: The Blue Voice
quests.description: Something under the calving face has been sounding one note for eleven years. You are close enough now to hear it without the ice in the way.

objectives.description: Get inside the Blue Caves.
Get past the seam that is not frozen.
Find the thing that will not stop ringing.

quests.name: The Count of the Strand
quests.description: Eleven years of skulls arriving facing the wrong way, and a ribcage on the shore that is the right shape only from a distance.

objectives.description: Get inside the Ribcage.
Answer what the door is asking for.
Find what has been doing the cutting.

quests.name: What the Marker Points At
quests.description: A bearing cut before the moot kept records, pointing down, at a hole with stonework around it that faces inward.

objectives.description: Get down the Moulin.
Read the seal from the side it was cut for.
Meet what the seal was written for.

quests.name: The Ninth Course
quests.description: Eight courses cut and nine weighed, every year for two hundred years, and the ninth arrives in the night out of a pan floor that rings.

objectives.description: Get under the eighth pan.
Find the way the ninth course comes up.
Find what has been drawing.

quests.name: What the Cistern Was For
quests.description: A hollowed rock the size of a market with a channel out of it and no channel in, and forty feet down the channel is damp.

objectives.description: Get into the channel.
Open what the keeper's office was for.
Find what has been drinking.

quests.name: The Bath That Is Still Full
quests.description: One warm bath in a desert, never metered by a city that meters to the cup, and masonry under poured glass on the crater lip.

objectives.description: Get down the crater stair.
Read the lines in the glass from the side they were cut for.
Find what has the fire under it.

quests.name: The Town That Came Back
quests.description: A dune that moved a mile in one season, off a town two hundred years too young for it, with every door barred from the street.

objectives.description: Get into the uncovered town.
Lift one of the bars.
Meet what the bars were on the outside for.

quests.name: The Warm Ground
quests.description: A village that has never been cold, over a tube that runs level for a mile and then turns up past stone the lava went round.

objectives.description: Get up the turn.
Get past the dressed stone.
Find what has been breathing.

quests.name: Under the Roofs
quests.description: Nine feet of ash in a single night, two houses dug and no bodies in either, and every door barred from inside.

objectives.description: Get under the roofs.
Open a door that was barred from inside.
Find what stayed.

quests.name: The New Treeline
quests.description: Eleven years of growth with forty rings in it, over workings somebody sealed from the inside.

objectives.description: Get into the old workings.
Get past a bar on the far side.
Find what has been counting.

quests.name: The Sheet
quests.description: A mile of glass poured flat over writing that is still legible, and something under it hot for nine hundred years.

objectives.description: Get down the cut.
Read what the glass went over.
Meet what has held the heat.

quests.name: The Knees
quests.description: Straight rows of cypress knees converging over open water, half of them cut level and healed over forty years ago.

objectives.description: Get to where the rows meet.
Open a way with the one edge that will.
Find what has been cutting them level.

quests.name: The Toll That Is Still Collected
quests.description: Two hundred years of a balanced ledger in one unbroken hand, for a shilling a head nobody has ever seen taken.

objectives.description: Get into the counting room.
Open what the ledger says is there.
Meet the collector.

quests.name: What the Hermit Was Watching
quests.description: Ninety years of tally marks up a door post, a fire pit still in use, and a hut built facing away from everything except one island.

objectives.description: Get onto the deep hummock.
Read what the marks were counting.
Meet what ninety years of watching was for.

quests.name: The Marker That Does Not Move
quests.description: Two hundred years on one bearing in a channel that redraws every spring, held by something that divers say is not rock.

objectives.description: Get alongside her at slack water.
Get under her.
Find what has been holding her.

quests.name: What the Terns Know
quests.description: Forty thousand pairs on the Bank, not one in the cut, and sand in the cut that will not freeze.

objectives.description: Get into the cut.
Get under the sand.
Find what the birds are avoiding.

quests.name: The Deep Wreck
quests.description: Guns run out at an island with nothing on it, and every hatch dogged from the outside.

objectives.description: Get onto her deck.
Get a hatch open.
Meet what they shut in.

quests.name: The Quarry's Second Face
quests.description: One warrant, two faces, eleven years of unlicensed carts going south at night, and a shored cut at the bottom of the wrong one.

objectives.description: Get to the second face.
Get into the hill.
Find what the fine stone was cut for.

quests.name: What Goes Under Aurenhal
quests.description: Brick newer than the city and older than the gate, warm air off the river, and one sheet missing from four hundred years of drains.

objectives.description: Get down the undercity grate.
Get past the third turn.
Find what has been keeping it warm.

quests.name: The Ford Toll
quests.description: A sluice worked to the day for ninety years by a keeper the parish stopped paying, over a chamber nobody has opened.

objectives.description: Get into the sluice house.
Get under the gate.
Meet the keeper.

quests.name: What the Bridge Was Built Over
quests.description: Footings rather than abutments, on a chasm four hundred years of dropped lights have not found the bottom of, older than the span laid onto them.

objectives.description: Get down into the footings.
Get past a bar on the far side.
Find what has been humming.

quests.name: The Ninth Column
quests.description: Eight columns holding a roof and a ninth holding nothing, weeping warm salt water four hundred miles from any sea.

objectives.description: Get to the columns.
Open what the ninth column is.
Find what has been weeping.

quests.name: The Lamps That Are Still Lit
quests.description: Four hundred unoiled years of light, at a spacing no road needs, over marks on the floor you can only read in the dark between them — and a stair with a course lifted out from below.

objectives.description: Get to the ninth landing.
Read what is cut on the risers.
Meet what lifted the course out.

quests.name: The Scouring
quests.description: A chalk figure three parishes clear every spring without knowing why, that reads as lines from the cliff and has corners in it.

objectives.description: Get under where the lines cross.
Lift the turf the way it has been lifted before.
Find what cut them square.

quests.name: The Tower That Still Signals
quests.description: No roof, no stair, and every skipper on this coast correcting two points to starboard off the head after dark.

objectives.description: Get in under the head on the tide.
Open what the tower was worked from.
Meet what has been keeping the correction true.

quests.name: One a Year, Unclaimed
quests.description: Two hundred years of one entry each October — taken up, never collected — and the fee paid in coin by somebody.

objectives.description: Be in the yard on the night.
Open the wall that was here first.
Meet what has been taken up every year.

quests.name: The Extra Miles
quests.description: Fourteen marked miles on an eleven-mile road, and the three that do not fit sight along a line of their own.

objectives.description: Get down into the sunken lane.
Work out which three marks are the extra ones.
Find what has been walking them.

quests.name: The Road Nobody Cut
quests.description: Forty yards wide and nine miles straight through a wood that closes any gap in four years, and nothing crosses it at night.

objectives.description: Get to the only thing built on it.
Open the dry arch under the bridge.
Meet what uses it after dark.

quests.name: The Round
quests.description: Four hundred years of quarterly payment to a woodward nobody can name, and marks that have moved eighty yards outward.

objectives.description: Get to the mark cut all the way through.
Walk the round with the rod that measures it.
Meet whoever has been earning the fee.

quests.name: The Planting
quests.description: Eleven miles of one species set in a single season, running the wrong way to break any wind that blows here.

objectives.description: Get to the stone in the middle of it.
Settle the count that will not settle.
Find what the line was set around.

quests.name: What the Bank Shows
quests.description: A quarter-mile bed for a four-week river, and forty feet down in the open face, courses that were laid level.

objectives.description: Get down the open face.
Take a block out of the laid course.
Meet what the course was built to carry.

quests.name: The Last Water
quests.description: A spring that has never failed at the edge of a country where nothing runs, warm and tasting of iron, with a shored way down beside it.

objectives.description: Get to the top of the shoring.
Get past the timber somebody ordered.
Meet what has been keeping the water warm.

quests.name: Nine Hundred and One
quests.description: Two stairs where the hold admits to one, swept daily by nobody on any payroll, and a count that will not agree with the lintel.

objectives.description: Get onto the flight nobody uses.
Find which step is the one too many.
Meet whoever has been sweeping them.

quests.name: Rung From Below
quests.description: A bell for a shut road, rung eleven times on an open one, with the rope worn on the face a hand cannot reach.

objectives.description: Get into the house that goes further.
Match the eleven nights to what was under them.
Meet what has been pulling from underneath.

quests.name: The Breathing Face
quests.description: A cave that draws and blows to the minute, warm, out of a north face that has never thawed.

objectives.description: Get into the mouth on the draw.
Get past where the survey stops.
Meet what has been doing the breathing.

quests.name: Colder's Fire
quests.description: Two hundred years alight on a third of the fuel it needs, kept for a man the parish register buries twice.

objectives.description: Get into the cold room underneath.
Find which two nights have no name against them.
Meet what the fire has been feeding.

quests.name: Forty-One Out, Forty-One In
quests.description: Every body the deep peat gave up written down as returned, and not always the one that was taken.

objectives.description: Get below the band nobody cuts past.
Work out which two went back different.
Meet what has been doing the returning.

quests.name: The Drive That Goes Over
quests.description: A roofless shooting house with this century's wear in eight even places, and a beaters' line drawn over the scarp and down.

objectives.description: Get under the scarp where the line goes.
Take the eighth place in the line.
Meet what the drive has been driving.

quests.name: The First Door
quests.description: Hesper's list says the first of the eight was opened under a ward-house in the Skarnspine, and that the bar on its cellar door is on the inside.

objectives.description: Get down to the ward cellars.
Get past a bar that was put up from inside.
Finish what came through the first door.

quests.name: The Second Door
quests.description: The moor took Barrowgate's keep back four hundred years ago. Something has been keeping the undercroft dry the whole time.

objectives.description: Get into the undercroft.
Finish what came through the second door.

quests.name: The Third Door
quests.description: A root cellar in the Hollow Beeches with a floor under the floor, and the Keepers' third line struck through in red by a hand that was not Hesper's.

objectives.description: Get into the root cellar.
Finish what came through the third door.

quests.name: The Fourth Door
quests.description: Eight hundred feet of quarry gallery along a seam that stops at forty, ending at a face nine generations of quarrymen worked around and never into.

objectives.description: Get into the quarry galleries.
Open the face the quarry never cut.
Finish what came through the fourth door.

quests.name: The Fifth Door
quests.description: The Black Water covered a hall. The hall is still furnished, still arranged, and still occupied by one thing that was sitting down when the water came.

objectives.description: Get into the sunken hall.
Finish what came through the fifth door.

quests.name: The Sixth Door
quests.description: A milepost on a road that measures nothing, with four hundred feet of dressed vault under it and one way down.

objectives.description: Get into the vault under the milepost.
Finish what came through the sixth door.

quests.name: The Seventh Door
quests.description: A room four miles down the Long Hall, dressed to the inch, with no furniture and no purpose except to hear — and it has heard everything that ever walked past it, including you.

objectives.description: Get into the listening room.
Stop it listening.
Finish what came through the seventh door.

quests.name: The Eighth Door
quests.description: The vent-readers have signalled past the Signal Deep for six hundred years and never once signalled to it, and not one of them was ever told not to.

objectives.description: Get down into the Signal Deep.
Finish what came through the eighth door.

quests.name: The Ninth Line
quests.description: Nine doors opened in order over eleven hundred years is not weather and it is not luck. Somebody has been keeping the count, and the count does not stop at nine.

objectives.description: Get under the ring in the Witchwood.
Finish whatever has been keeping the count.

arcs.name: The Open Door
arcs.description: A parish matter that turns out not to be one.

arcs.name: The Three Wards
arcs.description: Nine were built. Three are already open. You can be at two of the rest in time, and not at all three.

arcs.name: The Eel-Weir
arcs.description: A fish turned round in Harvest, and the reason it turned round has been under the hedge country for rather longer than that.

arcs.name: Bone Alley
arcs.description: Three of the guild went down at Kettle Yard and did not come up, and the reason had been bricked up in the west range for sixty years.

arcs.name: What the Strand Keeps
arcs.description: A ship on the bar, a kiln that was cold for sixty years and not on the night that mattered, and an argument about the difference between a wreck and a cargo.

arcs.name: The Ledger and the Light
arcs.description: Four hulls in nine years off one headland, and a hall full of men who make a living being right about exactly this.

arcs.name: The Hermit of the Beeches
arcs.description: Two years of a man in a tree telling the moot that the wood is moving, and two years of the moot having something more pressing on.

arcs.name: The Diggers' Camp
arcs.description: Four hundred feet of barrow with two ends, and four hundred years of everybody agreeing to dig the same one.

arcs.name: The Dry River
arcs.description: A well that stopped in a season, eleven wagons pointed at it, and four hundred years of a grazing right that nobody has written down.

arcs.name: The Cut
arcs.description: Nine days of red water, two days of none, and nine hundred years of ledgers with the answer on two pages nobody had put together.

arcs.name: The Throat
arcs.description: Eleven days of a chain hanging still that has never hung still for more than two, and eleven people whose whole office is knowing what that means.

arcs.name: The Drowned Bell
arcs.description: A church that went under in one night in the year six-eleven, a tower built four hundred yards inland by people who had learnt something, and a bell that has been heard since.

arcs.name: The Old Seams
arcs.description: Nine hundred years of a hold writing everything down, and four years in the middle of it that nobody wrote anything about at all.

arcs.name: The Rot
arcs.description: Two hundred years of pickers holding a line at the fifth gallery, and one season that put them back to the second.

arcs.name: The Ninth Well
arcs.description: Nine shafts sunk in one season by one crew, eight of them on the roster, and a camp laid out for four hundred years so that nobody faces the other one.

arcs.name: The Last Cairn
arcs.description: Eleven hundred cairns counted from one, for nine hundred years, by people who have never once opened it.

arcs.name: The Drowned Fort
arcs.description: Guns run out and a dry magazine on the same night, and four crews since who went to find out which came first.

arcs.name: The Frostmere, Unaccounted
arcs.description: Three things the Landing has known about for years and never once written down.

arcs.name: The Glasslands, Unmetered
arcs.description: Four ways of noticing that the water did not leave on its own.

arcs.name: The Ember Reach, Unread
arcs.description: Four arguments the vent-readers have been losing for a century, and the ground agreeing with them the whole time.

arcs.name: Thornmere, in Account
arcs.description: Three sets of books the marsh has been keeping, none of them for anybody who asked.

arcs.name: The Isles, Off the Chart
arcs.description: Three things the sea has been consistent about, in a place where the sea is consistent about nothing.

arcs.name: The Kingsvale, Unwarranted
arcs.description: Three things the Crown's paperwork does not cover, within two days' walk of where you started.

arcs.name: The Deeproads, Unsurveyed
arcs.description: Three things the Wayfinders have measured for four hundred years and never once written down.

arcs.name: The Silver Coast, Surveyed
arcs.description: Three pieces of work somebody did carefully along this coast and never filed with anybody.

arcs.name: The Duskwood, on Terms
arcs.description: Three arrangements this forest was made to accept, all of them still being honoured by somebody.

arcs.name: The Sunward Steppe, Laid Out
arcs.description: Three pieces of work under nine hundred years of grass, all three of them still doing what they were built to do.

arcs.name: The Skarnspine, Kept
arcs.description: Three pieces of upkeep on a mountain that has a hold on it, none of them the hold's.

arcs.name: The Weeping Moor, Returned
arcs.description: Three counts this moor has been keeping, and all three of them balance, which is the trouble.

arcs.name: The First Three
arcs.description: Three of the eight doors nobody was watching, and what walked out of them while everybody was looking at the ninth.

arcs.name: The Middle Three
arcs.description: Three doors somebody found before the Keepers did, and put four hundred feet of careful stone over without ever saying why.

arcs.name: The Ninth Line
arcs.description: The last two doors, and the thing that had been opening them in order and writing down how many were left.

arcs.name: The Unsealing
arcs.description: Nine doors were shut on purpose. Somebody has been opening them in order, and the ninth is the last.

lore.name: Whales used to calve inside the face. They have not come inside it in eleven years, and they still come to the shore either side.
It is not a noise. It is a note — one note, the way a struck bowl goes on after you have stopped touching it.
It only sounds while the ice is making. In a thaw there is nothing down there at all, and men have gone in during a thaw and found out why that is no comfort.
The Landing stood a mile further in, once. They moved the whole of it in a single winter and wrote down nothing about why.
There are more skulls on the Strand than the Landing has ever had ships. Somebody has been counting for eleven years and the number keeps going the wrong way.
Half of them are cut. Not flensed — cut, with something that went through bone in one stroke and left no chatter at the edge.
They are facing inland. Every one of them. A whale that dies at sea does not arrive facing inland.
The bones standing up out of the Strand are not one animal. They are the right shape from the water and the wrong shape from inside, and the difference is somebody's work.
lore.source: cut into the strand camp's door

lore.name: The marker on the Glass Ice is a bearing, and the bearing has no cairn at the end of it. Every other marker on the Reach points at a cairn.
It was cut before the moot kept records, which is a way of saying nobody alive knows who set it or what they were pointing at.
It does not point across. Stand where the cutter stood and it points *down*, and there is only one hole in the Glass Ice.
Whatever is at the bottom was shut in, not shut out. The stonework faces the wrong way to be keeping anything from getting down.
lore.source: the stone rows on the Flats

lore.name: The pans are cut in eight courses. Every salt town on this coast cuts eight, because eight is what one season of sun will draw.
The weighing house has counted nine courses out of these pans every year for two hundred years, and nobody has ever cut a ninth.
The ninth is heavier and it does not taste of this sea. The weigher keeps a jar of it and will not sell any.
Whatever the ninth course is, it arrives between one evening and the next morning, and no water runs into the pans in the night.
The cistern is bigger than the market it sits under and has been dry since before anybody's grandmother. The village is named after it anyway.
It was cut, not built. One rock, hollowed, and the tool marks run the wrong way for anyone standing on the floor of it.
There is a channel out of it and no channel into it, which is a thing a cistern does not have.
The channel out is damp forty feet down, in a place that has not had rain in nine years.
Every well in the city is metered by the wardens, to the cup. The bath under the Glass Quarter has never once been metered.
It is warm, and nothing else in the Glasslands is warm. Warm water in a desert means it came from somewhere with a fire under it.
The cutters make one lens they will not sell and will not explain, and they have made it every year for longer than the guild has minutes for.
lore.source: an apprentice at the Cutters' Hall

lore.name: The crater is not a crater. There is stonework under the glass on the lip and it goes down further than anybody has measured.
lore.source: cut into the shrine on the lip

lore.name: The dune moved off that town in a single season. Dunes here move a pace a year and that one moved a mile.
The town is the wrong age for the dune. It should have been under it for nine hundred years and it has been under it for two hundred.
Every door in it is barred from the outside, and they were barred before the sand came.
There is glass in the streets that was not made in a kiln and did not come from lightning. It runs in lines, and the lines lead somewhere.
The ground under the village has never been cold. Not in a winter, not in the two years the mountain was quiet, not once.
A tube burnt out by lava runs downhill, because that is what the lava was doing. The one under the village runs level for a mile and then turns up.
Air comes out of it in the same rhythm all year, and it is not the mountain's rhythm. The mountain has seasons. This does not.
There is dressed stone in the tube a quarter-mile in, and the lava went round it rather than over it.
The roofs of the buried village are the wrong way up. Ash does not lift a roof; it presses one.
They dug two houses out in living memory and found no bodies in either. A village that had time to leave does not bar its doors.
One fall of ash, one night, and nine feet of it. The Reach has never done nine feet in a night before or since.
The drifts over that village are warm to the hand a foot down, and the rest of the Ashfall is stone cold.
The March burned to bare rock and had a treeline again in eleven years. Ninety is the number, everywhere, always.
The rings in them are wrong. Eleven years of growth and forty rings, and the rings run the wrong way out from the middle.
Whatever they were mining under the March was shut up, and it was shut from the inside. There is no way to bar that door from the adit side.
The iron posts along the road are not milestones. They are set at the corners of something, and the something is under the trees.
lore.source: a carter on the Smoking Road

lore.name: A mile of glass, poured flat. Lava does not pour flat; it pools and it cracks and it goes where the ground takes it.
The stair into it was not melted through. It was cut, and then the glass came up around the cut.
There is writing under the sheet, a foot down, and it is legible, which means the glass went over it gently.
Whatever is under it is still hot after nine hundred years, and nothing on the Reach has held heat that long.
Cypress knees come up where the roots run, which is to say anywhere. In the deep maze they are in rows, and the rows are straight.
The rows converge. Follow two of them far enough and they meet, and they meet over the water rather than at a tree.
Half of them are cut off level at the top, and the cuts have healed over, which takes forty years. Nobody has worked that maze in a hundred.
There are no leeches in the deep maze. There are leeches in every other inch of this marsh.
The toll house on the causeway has taken nothing in two hundred years. The Crown stopped manning it when the causeway sank.
Somebody still sends a ledger in every year, and every year it balances, and the takings on it are a shilling a head.
It has been the same hand for two hundred years. Not a copied hand — the same one, with the same slant and the same broken g.
Nobody has ever seen it collected and nobody who walks the causeway is short a shilling afterwards. Something is paying.
There is a hut on the far hummock with a fire pit that has been used and nobody in this marsh can name who lives in it.
Ninety years of tally marks up the door post, five and five and five, and the newest of them are not weathered.
The hut faces away from the water and away from the road, which leaves one island, and that is a thing to build a hut looking at.
The channels near it run warm, and warm water in this marsh means the water is coming up rather than down.
Everything in the Narrows moves. Banks shift a cable a winter and the pilots redraw every spring. One wreck has been on the same bearing for two hundred years.
She is iron-fastened, and nobody was iron-fastening hulls when she went down. She is either much younger than the wreck or much older than the practice.
She is not aground. Divers have been under her twice and she is held, and what she is held by is not rock.
The bearing she keeps is not the channel. Laid off properly it runs through the Bank and out the far side.
lore.source: cut into the pilot station's rail

lore.name: Forty thousand pairs nest the Bank and not one pair nests the cut. Terns will nest on a wreck, on a gun, on a corpse.
They came off the cut in one year, within living memory, and they had nested it for as long as anybody kept count before that.
Nothing calls in the cut. Forty thousand birds a hundred yards off and the cut is silent, which is a thing you can hear.
The sand in the cut does not freeze. Nothing else on the Bank stays unfrozen and it does not.
She went down with her guns run out. A ship that founders does not have her guns run out; a ship that was fighting does.
There is nothing on the reef for her to have been fighting. No second wreck, no shot in the rock, nothing.
Every gun that is still run out is run out to one side, and that side is the island.
Her hatches are dogged from outside. Somebody shut the crew in and then the ship went down with her guns out.
The quarry has been worked from two faces. The Crown's warrant is for one, and the tallies are for one, and there are two.
The stone off the second face is not roadstone. It is finer, and there is none of it in any road in the Kingsvale.
The gibbet on the Kingsroad was put up the year the second face opened, and the assize rolls have nobody hanged on it.
Carts went south off that road at night for eleven years and the posting house has every one of them in the book, unlicensed.
The undercity is bricked off at the third turn. The brick is newer than the city and older than the King's Gate.
Air comes out of that grate all year and it is warmer than the river, which the river should not permit.
The Library has the city's drains back four hundred years, and the sheet for the year the brick went in is missing from the run.
The Long Wharf was rebuilt on new piles in the same year, and the old piles are still down there in the mud, cut off level.
There is a keeper's cottage on the end of the gear at Pennyford, with a roof and a door that shuts, and the parish has not paid a keeper in ninety years.
The sluice is worked. It is up in the spring and down at the harvest, every year, on the day.
The inn is called the Drowned Ox for an ox that drowned at a ford eleven inches deep, which is a thing an ox cannot do.
There is a stone in the ford bed with a hole through it, and the hole is worn by rope, and nobody has tied anything there in living memory.
Nobody has oiled the market road in four hundred years. The lamps along it are lit.
They are set at a spacing no lamp needs. Twice as far apart as you would light a road, and exactly as far apart as each other.
Three of them are out, and the three that are out are the three nearest the toll post.
They do not light the road evenly. Stand in the dark between two and the floor has marks on it that you cannot see under a lamp.
The chasm has no bottom that anybody has found, and the Wayfinders have dropped lights down it for four hundred years.
A bridge over a bottomless chasm has abutments, which lean on the cliff. The Black Bridge does not have abutments. It has piers, and a pier stands on something.
The span is dwarf work and what it rests on is not. The lower stonework is older, and the span was laid onto it.
The bridge hums in a wind there is no wind for. It has done since before Karn Dolur, and the dwarves will not discuss it.
The vault weeps, and what runs off its stonework is warm. Nothing else this deep is warm.
There is a shaft up out of the vault, and it goes up further than there is rock above it before you reach the sky.
Nine pillars in the vault. Every hall in the Deeproads is built in eights, and the wayfinders' survey has that hall in eights too.
The water weeping out of the vault's stonework is salt, and there is no sea within four hundred miles of straight down.
Three parishes turn out to clear the chalk every spring, and every one of them will tell you they only come because the other two do.
From four hundred feet up and two miles along it does not read as an animal at all. It reads as lines, and two of them cross square.
The turf is let grow everywhere on that hill but one shape, and the shape has corners in it. Nothing that runs has corners.
There is standing water on the top of a chalk hill that has never once gone dry, in a drought, above the water table. Somebody built that, and building it took the same summer as the cutting.
Every skipper working out of the three villages comes two points to starboard off the head after dark, and not one of them can tell you what they are correcting for.
There is no stair in it and no floor above the second course, and a light has been seen in the top of it four times in living memory, always in the same week of the year.
Forty thousand birds on that headland, and a circle of bare rock forty feet across at the tower's foot where nothing has ever nested.
The way in under the head opens at the bottom of a spring tide and stays open about an hour, which is not long enough to go in and come back out again.
The bailiff's book has one entry a year and has had for two hundred years: the same night in October, one taken up, never collected.
The yard is dry-stone on three sides and mortared on the fourth, and the mortared face is older than the town by a very long way.
The coach horses will not stand in that yard on that night, and the stablers gave up arguing with them about it two generations ago.
The fee is paid every October, in coin, into the parish box, for a beast nobody ever comes for. The parish stopped asking who pays.
There are fourteen marked miles on a road that is eleven miles long, and the wayhouse book has counted it that way since it was opened.
Three of the marks do not sit on the road at all. Sighted from one another they make a straight line of their own, crossing it.
The oaks were not planted. Every one of them is a cutting off the same tree, which you can see in the leaf, and that tree is not on this road.
There is a lane out that way worn six feet down into the ground. It takes a hundred years of carts to wear a lane that deep and nothing has used it in living memory.
Forty yards wide and dead straight for nine miles, in a wood that shuts a cart track in four years if you stop using it.
Every tree along its edge is the same age, and none of them is old. Something clears it, and clears it often enough that nothing gets big.
The bridge on it crosses nothing. The stream moved two hundred years ago and the bridge is still pointed, still sound, and somebody is still keeping it that way.
Nothing crosses it after dark. Not the deer, which will cross a turnpike. They go up it or down it, and they do not go over.
The parish has paid a woodward every quarter for four hundred years and nobody at Fenny Cross can tell you the name of the current one.
The last field ends where it has always ended. The marks on the edge of the wood are eighty yards further out than the survey puts them, and the survey is not wrong.
The burners will not cut inside a line every one of them can walk you along and not one of them can account for.
Every stone on the edge has been re-cut on the same face, and the cuts are fresh, and there is nobody the parish is paying to do it.
Eleven miles of it, one species the whole way, and every tree in it was set within a season of every other. That is a season's work for four hundred people.
The wind here comes off the south-west and has for as long as anybody has grazed here. The line runs south-west to north-east. It breaks nothing at all.
The Lines have kept a record of every foaling, every crossing and every death for nine hundred years, and there is no entry anywhere for eleven miles of trees.
Count them going north and count them coming back and you will not get the same number, and you will not get it twice running either.
A quarter of a mile across, for a river that runs four weeks in the year. Nothing that runs four weeks a year cuts a bed that wide.
Forty feet down in the open face there are courses of dressed stone. Not fallen in and not washed down — laid, level, and going on into the bank both ways.
The flood comes in the same week every year and the Lines move stock three days ahead of it. Ask any of them how they know and they will say the grass tells you, and they will not be able to say how.
There has been a camp at that crossing for nine hundred years, and the crossing is dry eleven months and impassable the twelfth. Nobody has ever needed to camp there.
The spring at the edge of the pale ground has not failed in nine hundred years of record, and two miles further on nothing has run at all since before anybody was counting.
It comes up warm and it tastes of iron. Every other water on this grass comes up cold and tastes of grass.
Whatever goes down beside it is shored, with timber, properly. Shoring is a mine's work and there has never been a mine on this steppe.
The Lines will water there and will not camp there, and they have twelve reasons between them and no two of the twelve agree.
Nine hundred steps, cut and railed, and swept every day of the year. The hold pays a great many people and not one of them for that.
There are two of them. The broken one is older, and it was cut by a hand that worked to a different tread — shorter, deeper, and not for legs the length of ours.
Walk it and count and you get nine hundred and one. The hold's own measure, cut into the gate lintel, says nine hundred.
Nothing nests in the shade of the older one. On a gritstone face, in this country, that is the strangest sentence anybody has said to you all week.
It is rung when the road is shut. The watch book has it rung eleven times on a night the road was open, and each time the watch was asleep and each time the watch was believed.
The rope is worn on the inside of the turn, which is the face a hand does not touch. Something has been pulling it from a direction nobody stands in.
Nine houses dug into the slope, all of them a room and a half. One of them goes back seventy feet, and its people have never mentioned it, and their neighbours have never asked.
The forge's coal comes up out of the slope warmer than it went down into it, and the smith has stopped saying so out loud.
It draws and blows on a count you can keep with a watch. Weather does not keep time and this does, to the minute, in a gale or a calm.
What comes out is warmer than what goes in, on a face that is in shade from Emberfall to Greening and has never once thawed.
The road runs past its mouth and the ice will not form within forty feet of it, which the guides use and none of them will discuss.
Karn Dolur has mapped every hole in this mountain to the inch, and the survey stops at that mouth with a blank margin and no note saying why.
It has not been out in two hundred years. Colder kept it forty and the parish has kept it a hundred and sixty since, by rota, without one lapse anybody can find.
The parish buys peat for it by the load and the load it buys is about a third of what a fire that size eats. Nobody has ever been short.
Colder is in the register twice, buried forty years apart, in the same hand, with the same three words after the name.
Two nights a year, when the wind comes off the moor rather than the vale, it burns green and the whole village is indoors by dark without anybody having said so.
Forty-one have come out of the deep peat since the cutters started keeping count, and the store's book records forty-one put back.
They are not always the same ones. Two were noted as returned in a different condition than they went in, and the note is in the clerk's ordinary hand, as though it were ordinary.
The peat at that depth is eleven thousand years old. One of the forty-one had an iron buckle on it and iron is four thousand.
Nobody cuts below the black band, and every cutter here can find the black band in the dark, and not one of them was ever taught where it is.
The house has no roof and the flags in front of it are worn through in eight places, evenly spaced, and the wear is this century.
The beaters' line on the old estate map does not stop at the scarp. It is drawn over it and down, and the ink is the same ink.
Birds go out over that drop on one day of the year, in numbers, and the count that goes out is not the count that comes back, and it never has been.
The holes under the scarp draw upward. Every other hole on this moor breathes down, because cold air falls, which is a thing cold air does everywhere.

loreThreads.name: The Blue Voice
loreThreads.description: Something under the calving face has been sounding one note for eleven years, and the whales understood it before anybody else started listening.

loreThreads.name: The Count of the Strand
loreThreads.description: The boneyard has been growing faster than the fleet can explain, and one man has the tally.

loreThreads.name: What the Marker Points At
loreThreads.description: A bearing cut before the moot kept records, aimed at no cairn, and not aimed across.

loreThreads.name: The Ninth Course
loreThreads.description: Eight courses cut, nine weighed, every year for two hundred years, and the ninth does not taste of this sea.

loreThreads.name: What the Cistern Was For
loreThreads.description: A hollowed rock the size of a market, a channel out and no channel in, and forty feet down it is damp.

loreThreads.name: The Bath That Is Still Full
loreThreads.description: One warm bath in a desert, unmetered in a city that meters everything, and a lens the cutters make every year and will not sell.

loreThreads.name: The Town That Came Back
loreThreads.description: A dune moved a mile in one season and gave back a town two hundred years too young, with every door barred from outside.

loreThreads.name: The Warm Ground
loreThreads.description: A village that has never been cold, over a tube that runs level for a mile and then turns up.

loreThreads.name: Under the Roofs
loreThreads.description: Nine feet of ash in one night, no bodies in two dug houses, and every roof the wrong way up.

loreThreads.name: The New Treeline
loreThreads.description: Eleven years of growth with forty rings in it, over workings that were sealed from the inside.

loreThreads.name: The Sheet
loreThreads.description: A mile of glass poured flat over writing that is still legible, and something under it that has been hot for nine hundred years.

loreThreads.name: The Knees
loreThreads.description: Cypress knees standing in straight rows that converge over open water, half of them cut level and healed.

loreThreads.name: The Toll That Is Still Collected
loreThreads.description: Two hundred years of a balanced ledger in one unbroken hand, for a toll nobody has ever seen taken.

loreThreads.name: What the Hermit Was Watching
loreThreads.description: Ninety years of tally marks on a door post, a fire pit still in use, and a hut built facing the wrong way on purpose.

loreThreads.name: The Marker That Does Not Move
loreThreads.description: Two hundred years on one bearing in a channel that redraws every spring, held by something that is not rock.

loreThreads.name: What the Terns Know
loreThreads.description: Forty thousand pairs on the Bank, none in the cut, and sand in the cut that will not freeze.

loreThreads.name: The Deep Wreck
loreThreads.description: Guns run out on one side with nothing to fire at, and hatches dogged from outside.

loreThreads.name: The Quarry's Second Face
loreThreads.description: One warrant, two faces, and eleven years of unlicensed carts going south at night.

loreThreads.name: What Goes Under Aurenhal
loreThreads.description: Brick newer than the city and older than the gate, warm air off the river, and a missing sheet in the Library's run.

loreThreads.name: The Ford Toll
loreThreads.description: A sluice worked to the day by a keeper the parish stopped paying ninety years ago.

loreThreads.name: The Lamps That Are Still Lit
loreThreads.description: Four hundred years unoiled, burning, at a spacing no road needs, and three of them out at the toll post.

loreThreads.name: What the Bridge Was Built Over
loreThreads.description: Footings, not abutments, on a chasm with no bottom, older than the span laid onto them.

loreThreads.name: The Weeping Vault
loreThreads.description: Nine columns in a world built in eights, weeping salt water that is warm, under a shaft with too much rock above it.

loreThreads.name: The Scouring
loreThreads.description: A chalk figure three parishes clear every spring without knowing why, that reads as lines from above and has corners in it.

loreThreads.name: The Tower That Still Signals
loreThreads.description: A watchtower with no roof and no stair, off which every skipper on this coast corrects two points to starboard after dark.

loreThreads.name: One a Year, Unclaimed
loreThreads.description: Two hundred years of one entry each October — taken up, never collected — and the fee paid in coin by somebody.

loreThreads.name: The Extra Miles
loreThreads.description: Fourteen marked miles on an eleven-mile road, three of which sight along a line of their own.

loreThreads.name: The Road Nobody Cut
loreThreads.description: Forty yards wide and nine miles straight through a wood that closes any gap in four years, and nothing crosses it at night.

loreThreads.name: The Round
loreThreads.description: Four hundred years of paying a woodward nobody can name, and marks that have moved outward.

loreThreads.name: The Planting
loreThreads.description: Eleven miles of one species set in a single season, running the wrong way to break any wind that blows here, with no record anywhere of the work.

loreThreads.name: What the Bank Shows
loreThreads.description: A quarter-mile bed for a four-week river, and forty feet down in the open face, courses that were laid level.

loreThreads.name: The Last Water
loreThreads.description: A spring that has never failed at the edge of a country where nothing runs, warm and tasting of iron, with a shored way down beside it.

loreThreads.name: Nine Hundred and One
loreThreads.description: Two stairs where the hold admits to one, swept daily by nobody on any payroll, and a count that will not agree with the lintel.

loreThreads.name: Rung From Below
loreThreads.description: A bell for a shut road, rung eleven times on an open one, with the rope worn on the face a hand cannot reach.

loreThreads.name: The Breathing Face
loreThreads.description: A cave that draws and blows to the minute, warm, out of a north face that has never thawed.

loreThreads.name: Colder's Fire
loreThreads.description: Two hundred years alight on a third of the fuel it needs, kept for a man the parish register buries twice.

loreThreads.name: Forty-One Out, Forty-One In
loreThreads.description: Every body the deep peat gave up written down as returned, and not always the one that was taken.

loreThreads.name: The Drive That Goes Over
loreThreads.description: A roofless shooting house with this century's wear in eight even places, and a beaters' line drawn over the scarp and down.
